subfields: drug information centre and query handling

figures.notes: Simple tables and flowcharts only; slide images are not carried over.

audience.prior_knowledge: Pharmacology and basic clinical pharmacy are complete; no statistics background is assumed.
audience.display_line: For pharmacy students, Drug Information practical sections

goal.notes: Secondary course: the simplest useful edition; easy to study, valuable content (user). Each section is taught in 45 minutes at most. Fill the incomplete Section 2 and write four added chapters (3, 6, 9 and the missing Section 3 topic) from standard references, marked as added. Low effort by user instruction (2026-09-30).

size.restructuring_note: Ten chapters, one per 45-minute section, about 1,200-1,500 words (4-6 A4 pages) each: 1. The drug information centre; 2. Drug information sources (primary part added); 3. Study designs and levels of evidence (added); 4. Randomisation; 5. The research protocol, hypothesis and ethics; 6. Critical appraisal of a clinical trial (added); 7. Adverse drug reactions; 8. ADR causality assessment; 9. ADR reporting and pharmacovigilance (added); 10. Applied case: trauma. Chapter 10 turns the trauma case into an application of the whole course. Priority (user): an easy subject with valuable content.

mcq.format: Single best answer from four options (A-D); answers with one-line rationales.

references.style_note: Short list, 3-5 references per chapter. Core texts: Malone, Drug Information: A Guide for Pharmacists (latest edition); WHO pharmacovigilance and causality guidance; CONSORT; ICH-GCP.

must_not_change: No invented ISBN, publisher or copyright registration

output.fonts: Source Serif 4, Playfair Display, Alexandria (ltr-textbook-alexandria preset)
